key_insight: K/Rb-based double perovskites beta2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and strongly tunable from photovoltaic bandgaps to high thermoelectric performance as halogen changes from Cl to I.
engineering_relevance: These lead-free cubic halide perovskites are promising for safer solar absorbers, tandem/NIR optoelectronics, and waste-heat recovery materials.
method: DFT screening of structural stability, elastic properties, electronic bands, optical response, and thermoelectric metrics
Compared K and Rb variants across Cl, Br, and I compositions to map composition-dependent trends
Evaluated formation energy, tolerance factors, bandgaps, effective masses, lattice conductivity, and ZT
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust cubic stability for all six compounds, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV, and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: Results are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis quality, phase purity, and temperature-dependent defect effects still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
